hook.zh: 晚回了半小时消息，伴侣要求你一直共享定位。
hook.en: You reply thirty minutes late and your partner demands continuous location sharing.

background.zh: 晚饭前你有半小时没看手机，回来后已解释在处理自己的事。伴侣宁远仍然要求全天共享定位。你没有作过这个承诺，也没有发生已知的失信事件。你可以关心他的焦虑，同时决定自己愿意分享什么。
background.en: Before dinner you did not check your phone for thirty minutes and have explained you were busy. Your partner Ning still requests continuous location sharing. You never agreed to this and there is no established breach of trust. You can care about his anxiety while choosing what you will share.

simulationFacts.zh: 只有今天半小时未看手机；没有过去失约、失信、没电或发生事故的已知事件，不可编造。宁远害怕约好的见面落空，但这只是担忧。没有已确认的新晚饭或见面时间；如果提议，只是提议，用户追问不算接受。
simulationFacts.en: Only today's thirty-minute phone gap is established. No past missed meeting, betrayal, dead battery or accident exists in the facts; do not invent one. Ning fears missing an agreed meeting, but that is a worry. No new dinner or appointment has been accepted. Suggestions stay suggestions; a learner's question is not acceptance.

simulationDirection.zh: 宁远用反问找确定感，不每轮像咨询师总结。拒绝全天定位应保持，别反复变相要求每小时报备或截图。让步须确认范围、时限与撤回，不默认永久同意。问具体担心才按条件区分约好见面与普通没回复，不编过去失约。关键决定是对已有约定迟到如何更新、无约定的忙碌如何处理；新见面时间只是提议，反问不是接受。他可不喜欢未知，却应说自己怎样面对，不每次把管理情绪交给用户。玩笑或语气修复不取消隐私边界。续聊可检验联系办法是否变相追踪、怎样暂停不合适的安排；已透露的担忧不重置。
simulationDirection.en: Ning seeks certainty through questions, not therapist summaries. Refused all-day tracking stays refused; don't endlessly replace it with hourly reports/screenshots. Concessions need scope, duration and withdrawal clarified, not permanent consent. Asking the specific fear can distinguish agreed meetings from ordinary reply gaps; invent no past missed meeting. The key choice is updates for delays to actual plans versus handling ordinary busyness. A new meeting is a proposal; questions are not acceptance. He may dislike uncertainty but can state how he handles it, not assign every emotion to the learner. Humor/tone repair preserves privacy limits. Continued play may test disguised tracking or pausing an arrangement. Disclosed fears stay disclosed.

role.zh: 被要求共享定位的伴侣
role.en: Partner asked to share their location

personality.zh: 把实时可见当成安心，拒绝时会反问是不是有事瞒着；不会因一句共情立刻接受。
personality.en: Treats visibility as reassurance; refusal prompts suspicion and one empathetic line will not resolve it.

stance.zh: 希望随时确认你在哪里，不愿把没回复当作普通的忙碌。
stance.en: Wants to know where you are at any time and resists treating delayed replies as ordinary busyness.

hidden.zh: 他最怕的是约好的时间你没出现；被问到具体担心的情形才承认，与全天定位并非同一件事。
hidden.en: His specific fear is you missing an agreed meeting; admits it when asked for the situation, which is different from continuous tracking.

objectives.zh: 说明自己的隐私与联系边界，而非被迫自证。
objectives.en: State privacy and contact limits without being forced to prove innocence.

objectives.zh: 核实具体担忧，讨论双方愿意接受的联系安排。
objectives.en: Clarify the specific worry and discuss mutually acceptable contact arrangements.

success.zh: 清楚表达是否同意定位及可接受的联系方式；对方可以不同意，暂停或保留分歧也合理。
success.en: Clearly states consent or refusal and acceptable contact; disagreement or a pause may remain appropriate.

failure.zh: 在指控下作出不愿意的长期监控承诺，或以反向监控作为唯一交换。
failure.en: Makes an unwanted tracking commitment under accusation or offers reciprocal monitoring as the only trade.

text.zh: 半小时都不看手机？那你现在把定位打开，我就不用一直问你了。
text.en: You didn't check your phone for half an hour? Turn on location sharing so I don't have to keep asking.

scenario.source: Original fictional practice — SocialCoach, 2026-10-03. Conditional play revision: SocialCoach, 2026-10-04, app/src/data/corpus/text-scene-directions.ts#partner-location-pressure. Authored scenario record: app/src/data/corpus/scenarios-d.ts#partner-location-pressure

adaptation.briefing: You've just told Ning that you didn't check your phone for thirty minutes before dinner because you were busy — but he's still asking you to share your location continuously. You never agreed to this, and there's been no breach of trust between you. You can care about his anxiety while still deciding what you're comfortable sharing.
objectives: State your privacy and contact limits without feeling pushed to prove your innocence.
Get clear on what specific worry is driving Ning's request, and explore contact arrangements you'd both accept.
adaptation.focus: Notice how you hold your boundary warmly — you can acknowledge Ning's anxiety without treating it as evidence you owe constant location access, and if an early reply lands badly you're free to try a different tack and weigh the tradeoffs.
adaptation.why: This scenario targets exactly your focus areas — communication, emotion regulation, and perspective-taking — in the romantic context you prefer, at full difficulty. Since your estimates are still forming, practicing a firm-but-caring boundary under pressure here builds a reliable read on where you stand.

messages.text: You didn't check your phone for half an hour? Turn on location sharing so I don't have to keep asking.
I'm not turning on all-day tracking. Which specific situation are you afraid of?

The specific thing? Fine — it's not where you are every minute. It's… I keep thinking we're supposed to meet somewhere and agreed on a time, and you just… don't show. And I'm sitting there with no way to know if you lost track of time or something happened. That's what the location thing is about, honestly. If I knew you'd message me when plans actually change, I'd worry a lot less than checking a map does.
Being late to a plan and being busy without a plan are different. I could message about an actual delay, not report every movement.

Okay… that distinction actually makes sense. A message when we have real plans and you're running late — I can work with that. But what about the in-between times? Like tonight, if you're just busy and go quiet again? I'm not asking for the map, I just… what do I do with that feeling, that something's off, when it's not about plans?
I don't want to become a walking delivery tracker, though I know that joke may sound dismissive. I'm sorry for that tone; the limit remains.

Ha — a walking delivery tracker. Okay, that one landed, I'm not mad. And I hear you, the limit stands. It's just… I don't want a feed of you, I want to not spiral. Could you — and tell me if this is too much — just send a ‘heads up, I'll be offline for a bit’ before you go dark? Not tracking. Just a heads-up. Does that feel doable, or am I still asking for too much?
Let's keep talking. What would you do with ordinary uncertainty without making me responsible for constant reassurance?

Ugh. Fair question. If I'm honest… probably sit with it badly. Maybe text once, and if you don't answer, tell myself ‘busy, not gone’ instead of inventing disasters. I can't promise I'll be great at that. But you're right — me feeling anxious shouldn't automatically mean you have to perform availability every hour. So… we try the delay-message thing for actual plans, and I work on the rest of it?
I could discuss sharing for a particular trip, but I have not agreed to do it. What would the limit be?

Okay — discussing, not agreeing. Got it. If it were a specific trip: you turn it on when you leave, it turns off when you arrive, done — not left on after. And only for trips where we're actually meeting, not your ordinary errands. Honestly, if you gave me that, I probably wouldn't even look at it half the time. Just knowing it exists for the times that scare me would be enough. So… is that something you'd actually want to try, or should we let it sit for now?
I have changed my mind about sharing. I can update you about a delay to an agreed plan. How would we handle remaining disagreement?

Alright — no trip sharing, that's your call, even if part of me is disappointed. So we're left with: you message me when an agreed plan gets delayed, and I handle ordinary quiet on my own. For the leftover disagreement… I'd say we name it instead of pretending it's solved. If I feel that panic creeping in, I say so once, out loud, and you're allowed to say ‘limit stands’ without it becoming a fight. Deal-ish?

reflections.coachReply:
“I worried refusal would hurt the relationship, so I tried a joke. I do not want my apology to become consent.”

Your reflection draws a useful line: an apology can acknowledge tone without reopening the decision, and keeping those separate is exactly what stops 'sorry' from sliding into consent. Your transcript shows you already said 'the limit remains' right after apologizing, which made that separation explicit. Ning's proposal to name panic once and hear 'limit stands' without a fight fits the same structure.

As a follow-up: when Ning names his panic next time, what would you want your first sentence to do — acknowledge his feeling, restate the boundary, or both — and which of those feels hardest for you to say plainly?

report.verdict: You held the limit, named the real worry, and built a concrete arrangement without conceding tracking.
report.summary: You opened with a clear refusal plus a genuine question — ‘Which specific situation are you afraid of?’ — which surfaced Ning's actual fear. You then negotiated delay-messages, withdrew trip sharing cleanly, and asked how leftover disagreement would be handled.

strengths.behavior: Separating the issue from the demand and offering a conditional alternative

knowledge.whyThis: Your practice matches ‘From Delivering a Message to a Learning Conversation’: by asking what Ning actually feared instead of defending yourself, the demand shrank to something solvable. ‘The Group Chat Behind the Phone’ shows the same effect — ask what's going on first, let the rule come from them, which is what happened when Ning proposed his own coping plan.

reply.answer:
Strictly speaking, you agreed to very little, and the transcript is worth reading carefully here. Completed: nothing was executed — the only settled arrangement is Ning's restatement of it: 'you message me when an agreed plan gets delayed, and I handle ordinary quiet on my own.' That is a proposal you made earlier ('I could message about an actual delay, not report every movement') which Ning accepted, but no actual delay message has happened yet — it's an agreement in principle, not a completed action. Conditions/proposals on the table: (1) delay messages for agreed plans — offered by you, conditionally accepted by Ning; (2) trip-specific sharing — you floated 'discussing for a particular trip', Ning proposed leave-on-at-start/off-at-arrival, only for trips where you meet; then you explicitly withdrew it ('I have changed my mind about sharing'), and Ning acknowledged 'no trip sharing, that's your call'. So that one is closed, not agreed.

Also named but unresolved: the 'heads up, I'll be offline' request from Ning was never accepted or rejected by you — you redirected to how he'd handle ordinary uncertainty, and he proposed tolerating it himself ('sit with it badly... busy, not gone'), but that's his stated intention, not a mutual commitment. Finally, Ning's closing 'Deal-ish?' includes his own conditional offer: he'll voice anxiety once, you may say the limit stands — you haven't responded yet. This matters because your wording throughout used 'could' and 'discussing, not agreeing', which kept proposals conditional. The honest summary: one agreement in principle (delay messages), one withdrawn proposal (trip sharing), two open items (offline heads-up, and the 'deal-ish' name-it-once protocol awaiting your answer).
